$comment: Enumerated pre-existing nested-shape severity escalations, for scripts/check-nested-severity.py. This file is a GATE INPUT, not a filter: the check still examines and reports every sh:node / sh:qualifiedValueShape reference. The run fails when a site appears that is not listed here AND when a listed site stops appearing, so the list can only shrink, and shrinking it is an explicit committed edit. Each entry names the vocabulary that owns the fix. Sites are keyed by referring shape (a blank-node property shape is named by its owning IRI shape plus its sh:path) plus the parameter and the referenced shape; a site that changes SHAPE is a new fact and must fail the gate. Nothing here is acceptable in the long run -- each entry is a place where a constraint published at sh:Warning or sh:Info is reported to a consumer at the referring constraint's severity, which is sh:Violation unless declared otherwise.
$rule: SHACL defines conformance as an empty validation result and that definition does not consult severity, so a nested sh:Warning makes the value node non-conforming and the referring sh:node constraint fires at its own severity. The cure is to move the soft constraint onto a shape that reaches its classes by sh:targetClass, as clinical v1.17 did. Declaring sh:severity on the reference is NOT the cure: severity attaches to a shape rather than to one nested result, so it demotes the whole referenced shape, structural violations included.
$established: 2026-08-28, clinical v1.17 (spec). The six clinical:ClinicalDocumentShape sites this check was written for are fixed, not baselined.

Cure is the clinical v1.17 one: move the soft constraints onto a shape targeting both classes.
